title: T1102.003 — Web Service - One-Way Communication
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Web Service - One-Way Communication with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.

steps.title: Defender view
steps.caption: Attacker posts the command The attacker writes an encoded blob into the comment section of a public video or post. To a human reader it looks like spam or a strange username string. To the implant it is the next instruction set. Nothing touches your network yet; this step happens entirely on the attacker's side and on the platform
steps.defender: WAF, reverse-proxy and application logs record the request, payload and backend behavior.

steps.caption: Marker found and decoded The implant's parser finds the marker inside the page, pulls out the encoded blob, and decodes it into a task - for example a download or a recon command. No new network event. EDR shows a helper process writing a small temp file right after the fetch

steps.title: Defender view
steps.caption: Malware executes the task The implant runs the decoded task. It may download a payload from a separate server or gather host information. Nothing is sent back through the video platform. Correlate the order of events: page fetch first, then a child process and a connection to a different host. That ordering is the strongest signal

steps.title: Defender view
steps.caption: Next command - the one-way loop The attacker posts the next encoded comment. The implant fetches the same URL again and finds new content. This loop can repeat for weeks or months. Watch the response byte size drift upward while the URL stays identical. Fixed-interval repeats from a server are rare and loud
steps.defender: WAF, reverse-proxy and application logs record the request, payload and backend behavior.

steps.title: Defender view
steps.caption: Output leaves via a different channel If the attackers need results, the implant sends them later to a different server or cloud service. The one-way channel itself stays read-only. Tasking and exfiltration live on separate paths. Tie them together with host and time context, not by expecting one flow to do both

steps.title: Defender view
steps.caption: SOC reviews proxy history An analyst groups proxy records by source host. One host shows the same URL fetched at a steady, metronome-like beat, an odd user agent, and slow byte growth as comments accumulate. Group by host, not by URL. One host, one URL, many timestamps is the shape of one-way tasking
steps.defender: WAF, reverse-proxy and application logs record the request, payload and backend behavior.

steps.title: Defender view
steps.caption: Block, isolate, hunt The team blocks the content category at the proxy and isolates the host in EDR. Then it hunts the marker string across proxy history to find every other host that fetched the same page. Blocking the platform alone is not enough. Hunt the exact URL and the marker text to scope the incident
